tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Columbia, the Gem of the Ocean or The Red, White and Blue (קָלֹמְבִּיָּה! צִיץ נֵֽזֶר הַיָּם או אָדוֹם, לָבָן וּתְֿכֵֽלֶת) — a patriotic hymn by Thomas A'Becket, Sr. (ca. 1843)

tei:lg.tei:l: O Columbia! the gem of the ocean,
The home of the brave and the free,
The shrine of each patriot’s devotion,
A world offers homage to thee,
Thy mandates make heroes assemble,
When Liberty’s form stands in view,
Thy banners make tyranny tremble,
When borne by the red, white and blue.
When borne by the red, white and blue,
When borne by the red, white and blue,
Thy banners make tyranny tremble.
When borne by the red, white and blue
When war winged it wide desolation,
And threatened the land to deform,
The ark then of freedom’s foundation,
Columbia, rode safe thro’ the storm;
With her garlands of vict’ry around her,
When so proudly she bore her brave crew,
With her flag proudly floating before her,
The boast of the red, white and blue
Chorus: When borne by the red, white and blue...
The winecup, the winecup bring hither,
And fill you it true to the brim,
May the wreaths they have won never wither,
Nor the star of their glory grow dim!
May the service united ne’er sever,
But they to their colors prove true!
The Army and Navy forever
Three cheers for the red, white and blue
Chorus: When borne by the red, white and blue...
